rows.speaker: author

rows.claim: They say Yahya committed no sin and did not even intend one; a prophetic report exempts him from the ordinary case of people who intend or commit sin.

rows.anchor: قالت ذلك بطبع البشرية خوف الفضيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that she feared people would rush to say things that displease God, though she knew this was God's decree.
rows.anchor: لكراهتها أن يعصي الله بسببها إذ كان الناس يتسرعون إلى القول

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He takes her words hypothetically: if offered a choice before this event between death and facing it, she would have chosen death.
rows.anchor: لو خيرت قبل هذه الحال بين الموت أو الدفع إلى هذه الحال لاختارت الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before this can refer to the day, the time, or the whole event.
rows.anchor: {قبل هذا} أي: قبل هذا اليوم، أو هذا الوقت، أو هذا الأمر

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Nasy in Arabic is something discarded and not thought worth notice; al-Shanfara's poem describes something hidden.
rows.anchor: النسي في كلام العرب الشيء المطروح لا يؤبه له

rows.speaker: الأخفش وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: They define nasy as a trivial thing accidentally left behind or forgotten; Yunus cites a small object left when a group departs.
rows.anchor: النسي ما أغفل من شيء حقير ونسي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: They interpret نسي منسيا as abandoned and unmentioned.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: (نسيا: متروكا لا يذكر)

rows.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد
rows.claim: They interpret it as a discarded menstrual cloth or blood clot.
rows.anchor: عكرمة، والضحاك، ومجاهد: (حيضة ملقاة)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: منسيا is passive, either forgotten or left; the intensifying sense is that even a trivial object may be sought, so she wishes to be something no one seeks or remembers.
rows.anchor: النسي وإن كان حقيرا فقد يطلب ويذكر، فهي تقول ياليتني (¬3) كنت

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He says her mention would be forgotten, and no trace or sight of her remain.
rows.anchor: السدي: ({وكنت نسيا منسيا} أي نسي ذكري، ومنسيا أي: نسي أثري فلا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The reading nasiyan with fatḥ and nasy with kasr are dialectal variants; nasy also names the scraps discarded by a woman during menstruation.
rows.anchor: الفراء: (هما لغتان مثل: الجسر والجسر، والحجر والحجر، والوتر والوتر. والنسي: ما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says Gabriel heard Maryam's distress and called from below her, beneath the mound; al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and Qatada also identify Gabriel at the mountain's foot.
rows.anchor: سمع جبريل كلامها وعرف جزعها فناداها من تحتها أسفل منها تحت الأكمة

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
rows.claim: They identify the caller as Jesus; Wahb, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Zayd share this view.
rows.anchor: مجاهد، والحسن: (الذي ناداها عيسى)

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: If Jesus called her, his speech serves to show her the sign in him.
rows.anchor: أن يبين الله لها الآية في عيسى

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: He considers Jesus the more fitting caller because hearing him removes her loneliness and grief and answers possible accusations against her.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المنادي لها عيسى أشبه وأشد إزالة لما خامرها من الوحشة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: He prefers the reading مِن تحتها with fatḥ on mīm, taking the general word as referring specifically to Jesus.
rows.anchor: أبو علي: (وأن يكون المنادي لها عيسى أشبه وأشد إزالة لما خامرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Sari means a stream; he says its watercourse had dried up and God caused the water to flow for Maryam, as the majority of exegetes hold.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: (يريد السري الجدول، وكان ساقيه للماء قبل ذلك، ثم انقطع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He also interprets sari as Jesus, saying Jesus was a noble man; after recognizing that Arabs call a river sari, he returned to the river interpretation.
rows.anchor: الحسن أنه قال: (يعني عيسى عليه السلام، كان والله سريا من الرجال)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linguists agree that sari means a river or stream; Labid's verse is cited as evidence.
rows.anchor: هذا القول. ولا خلاف بين أهل اللغة أن السري: النهر بمنزلة الجدول)

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He explains under you as level with Mary's feet, consistent with the report that Gabriel struck the ground beneath her; another report says Jesus struck it and water emerged.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: (بحيال قدميك) (¬1). فجعل تحت هاهنا إسما للجهة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Alternatively, تحتك means below you in rank or position, not necessarily physically aligned with Maryam.
rows.anchor: لهذه الجهة، ولكن المعنى جعله دونك، وقد يقال: فلان تحتنا أي: دوننا

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the river subject to Mary's command, as Pharaoh's rivers were said to flow beneath him, meaning under his authority.
rows.anchor: جعل النهر تحت أمرها إن أمرته أن يجري جرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hazz means to shake; ilayki means draw it toward yourself, so Maryam should pull the trunk while shaking it.
rows.anchor: إليك} الهز معناه: التحريك (¬7)، يقال: هززته فاهتز، ومعنى {إليك} اجذبيه إليك

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: He treats the bāʾ in بجذع as extra, citing ordinary expressions and poetry; al-Farra agrees and adduces فليمدد بسبب.
rows.anchor: الأخفش: (الباء زائدة) (¬1). وهي تزاد كثيرا في الكلام

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wording means that by shaking the palm trunk its dates fall; a genitive construction has been omitted.
rows.anchor: أبو علي: (ويحتمل أن يكون معنى {وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة} أي: بهز

rows.speaker: المبرد، حكاية الزجاج
rows.claim: He construes the instruction as shaking the trunk so that ripe dates fall to Maryam.
rows.anchor: هزي إليك بجذع النخلة رطبا تساقط عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasāqaṭ is underlying tasāqaṭu with tāʾ assimilated into sīn, and here means fall; a poet's usage illustrates the form.
rows.anchor: {تساقط عليك} أي: تتساقط فأدغمت التاء في السين، وتساقط هاهنا بمعني: تسقط،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes the palm drop dates, with رطبا as the direct object.
rows.anchor: المعنى: تسقط عليك النخلة رطبا جنيا، وانتصب (رطبا) على أنه مفعول به

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: He reads تساقط in a shortened form, deleting the tāʾ assimilated by other readers.
rows.anchor: حمزة: تساقط، مخففا (¬4). حذف التاء التي أدغمها غيره،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parsing supplies an understood fruit of the palm and takes رطبا as a circumstantial accusative; the fruit is implied by mentioning the palm.
rows.anchor: يكون المعنى: تساقط عليك ثمرة النخلة رطبا، فيكون انتصاب رطبا على الحال،

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: They parse رطبا as specification or explanation because the verb is transferred from the dates to the palm, as in the palm dropping dates.
rows.anchor: الفراء، والزجاج (¬1) انتصب (رطبا) على التمييز والتفسير؛ لأن

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: His transmitted reading uses the tafāʿala pattern; sāqaṭ can mean caused to fall, as illustrated by a verse about an animal and dogs.
rows.anchor: حفص عن عاصم: تساقط على وزن تفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rutab is ripened dates, while jani means gathered or picked fruit.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: (رطبا) الرطب: الناضج من البسر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Maryam saw fronds, then fruit emerge and ripen in an instant from the barren stump; the dates fell safely in their husks and comforted her.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك طرفة عين قبل أن يرتد إليها طرفها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: She should eat dates, drink from the stream, and be comforted by Jesus.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: (من الرطب {واشربي} من السري {وقري عينا} يريد بعيسى)

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: He gives the forms قررت به عينا, أقر, قرة, and قرورا for taking comfort in someone.
rows.anchor: الكسائي: (قررت به عينا أقر، قرة، وقرورا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others give قررت and explain قرة as the state or thing that delights the eye.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم يقول: قررت، أقر، القرة المصدر،

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: He derives the expression from coolness: joyful tears are cool while grief's tears are hot.
rows.anchor: الأصمعي: (أقر مأخوذ من القر والقرة، وهما البرد، ومعنى أقر الله عينه

rows.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
rows.claim: He rejects al-Asmaʿi's explanation, saying every tear is hot whether from joy or grief.
rows.anchor: أحمد بن يحيى فأنكره، # وقال: الدمع

rows.speaker: جماعة من أهل اللغة
rows.claim: They explain it as God settling the eye with a beloved sight so the person rests from looking elsewhere; the idiom also describes finding what one's heart sought.
rows.anchor: سكن الله عينك بالنظر إلى ما تحب

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الشيباني
rows.claim: He says it means God lets the eye sleep, relieving wakefulness through joy; a line of poetry is cited for the sense of sleeping eyes.
rows.anchor: أقر الله عينه أنام الله عينه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The command means be at peace; عين is accusative as a specification after shifting the action from the eye to the woman, as in the cited construction in 4:4.
rows.anchor: الفراء: {وقري عينا} جاء في التفسير: طيبي نفسا، وإنما نصبت العين؛ لأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He analyzes ترين as a sequence of deleted hamzah, vowel transfer, contraction, deletion at the conditional, and the emphatic feminine ending; the final yāʾ is vowelled to avoid two sukūns.
rows.anchor: ترين كان في الأصل ترأيين فحذفت الهمزة كما حذفت من يرى وترى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He illustrates the feminine yāʾ before emphatic nūn with the parallel command اخشين زيدا.
rows.anchor: الزجاج: (وكذلك تقول للمرآة: اخشين زيدا)

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: He explains the singular feminine and plural forms: in خطاب الواحد the verb's final radical is deleted before the feminine yāʾ, while plural forms retain it; jussive and subjunctive forms delete their nūn as in other verbs.
rows.anchor: أبو علي الفارسي في "المسائل الحلبية"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction to speak is elliptical: if she sees anyone and is asked about her child, she should say she vowed a fast to the Merciful.
rows.anchor: فيه اختصار؛ لأن المعنى: فإما ترين من البشر أحدا فسألك عن ولدك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses fast here as silence; in Arabic fasting can mean abstaining from food or speech.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: (صمتا) (¬3). ومعنى الصوم في اللغة: الإمساك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Maryam abstained from speech, food, and drink.
rows.anchor: قتادة: (صامت من الكلام، والطعام، والشراب)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the ordinary devotional fast, including abstention from food: otherwise the added statement that she will not speak would be redundant, and a God-directed fast is abstention from food.
rows.anchor: ولو أريد بالصوم هاهنا الصمت فقط لم يحتج إلى قوله فلن أكلم اليوم

rows.speaker: السدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: They say some Israelites seeking extra devotion fasted from speech as well as food, keeping silent until evening.
rows.anchor: السدي، وابن زيد: (كان في بني إسرائيل من أراد أن يجتهد صام

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They say Maryam was permitted to announce her vow and then say nothing more.
rows.anchor: المفسرون: (كان قد أذن لها أن تقول: {نذرت للرحمن صوما فلن أكلم

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another view says she communicated only this much by gesture to show that she was abstaining from speech.
rows.anchor: كانت تقول هذا القدر إشارة بحيث يعرف أنها ممسكة عن الكلام

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن زيد ووهب
rows.claim: She was told to remain silent because she had no visible defense before people; the child would speak and clear her of the accusation.
rows.anchor: ابن مسعود، وابن # زيد، ووهب: (أمرت بالصمت؛ لأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of specifying humans is that Maryam could speak with angels.
rows.anchor: خصت الإنس لأنها كانت تكلم الملائكة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One account says Maryam left in the morning for the sunshine and returned at noon carrying Jesus, with conception and birth occurring within three daytime hours.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس في رواية: (خرجت مريم من عندهم ضحى تتشرق للشمس

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Another account says she gave birth unnoticed, waited forty days to recover from childbirth, then brought Jesus to her people, who wept because they were a righteous household.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: (أتت به قومها تحمله بعد أربعين يوما، وذلك أنها ولدت حيث

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Fary describes anything extraordinary, whether a remarkable thing or deed; here it means something astonishing.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة: (كل فائق من عجب أو عمل فهو: فري،

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج وأهل اللغة
rows.claim: They define al-fary as a great deed and cite the saying about Umar that no extraordinary man matched his achievement.
rows.anchor: الفراء [والزجاج وجميع أهل اللغة: (الفري: الأمر العظيم، يقال فلان يفري الفري]

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Maryam has brought something grave and reprehensible, unknown of her and her family; Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Suddi likewise define fary as a great matter.
rows.anchor: عظيما منكرا لا يعرف منك ولا من أهل بيتك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، رواية عطاء
rows.claim: One view identifies Aaron as a devout Israelite contemporary of Maryam; forty thousand mourners attended his funeral, all called Aaron.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (أن مريم كانت عابدة، وكان في بني

rows.speaker: قتادة وكعب وابن زيد
rows.claim: They say Aaron was a righteous Israelite whose name was invoked for those known for piety, so Maryam is addressed as his counterpart in chastity; a report from al-Mughira from the Prophet supports this.
rows.anchor: قتادة، وكعب، وابن زيد قالوا: (هارون رجل صالح من

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He identifies Aaron as Moses's brother and says Maryam was called his sister because she descended from his line, as a Tamimi may be called brother of Tamim.
rows.anchor: السدي: (عنوا هارون أخا موسى، ونسبت مريم إلى أنها أخته؛ لأنها من

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He says Aaron was Maryam's paternal half-brother and the most exemplary man in Israel.
rows.anchor: كان هارون أخا مريم من أبيها ليس من أمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that this Aaron was openly wicked and Maryam was compared to him reproachfully.
rows.anchor: كان فاسقا معلنا بالفسق فشبهت به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says the statement means that her father was not an adulterer and her mother was not an adulteress.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: (يريد زانيا) (¬1).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying adultery of her parents indirectly accuses Maryam: if they were not adulterers, where did her child come from?
rows.anchor: والمعنى في نفي الزنا عن أبويها تعريض بزناها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He paraphrases the rebuke as saying her father, brother, and household were righteous, yet she has committed something grave.
rows.anchor: أهل بيتك أخوك وأبوك صالحون وقد أتيت أمرا عظيما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Maryam gestured for the people to speak to Jesus while he was nursing; they looked at one another in surprise.
rows.anchor: تريد أن كلموه وهو يرضع فنظر بعضهم إلى بعض تعجبا منها

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He says Maryam gestured that they should speak with Jesus, as their response makes clear.
rows.anchor: أشارت إليه بأن يجعلوا الكلام معه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the cradle means lying in the lap as an infant.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: (يريد في الحجر رضيعا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cradle is a place prepared for a child to sleep; it may mean a lap or the familiar child's bed.
rows.anchor: والمهد: الموضع الذي يهيأ لينام فيه الصبي

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة وكثير من المفسرين
rows.claim: They treat كان as extra, yielding the sense how can we speak to a child in the cradle; a line from al-Farazdaq is offered as evidence.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة: ({كان} هاهنا حشو زائد

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another explanation takes كان to mean came to be or happened.
rows.anchor: قوم: ({كان} في معنى وقع وحدث)

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He says من is conditional and كان means is: whoever is an infant in the cradle, how can we speak to him?
rows.anchor: وأجود الأقوال أن يكون في معنى الشرط والجزاء

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: He rejects treating كان as omitted or as meaning occurred, and adopts al-Zajjaj's conditional reading: whoever is an infant in the cradle, how can we speak to him?
rows.anchor: ابن الأنباري: (لا يجوز أن يكون الكون ملغى، وهو عامل في الصبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus stopped nursing, turned toward the people, and pointed before speaking.
rows.anchor: فلما سمع كلامهم لم يزد على أن ترك الرضاع وأقبل عليهم بوجهه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Jesus first confessed his servitude and God's lordship.
rows.anchor: ابن # عباس: (أقر بالعبودية على نفسه، وبربوبية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God gave him the Book and made him a prophet reports a prior decree about what would happen later.
rows.anchor: الكتاب وجعلني نبيا} أي: حكم لي بإيتاء الكتاب والنبوة فيما قضى وسبق،

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: An alternative says Jesus already received knowledge of Torah, wisdom, and writing in the womb; his fully formed intellect made his infant speech a miracle.
rows.anchor: قوم: (أخبر عما حصل له؛ لأن الله تعالى علمه وهو في بطن

rows.speaker: عكرمة وجماعة
rows.claim: They hold the future-decree interpretation; Ibn Abbas in the report of ʿAta is associated with the alternative that Jesus already had this knowledge.
rows.anchor: عكرمة وجماعة (¬2). والثاني معنى قول ابن عباس في

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Jesus was made blessed by calling people to God, His oneness, and His worship.
rows.anchor: لأن أدعوا إلى الله وإلى توحيده وعبادته

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He explains blessed as teaching good and benefiting people.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: (جعلني معلما للخير نفاعا)

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another explanation says Jesus's blessing was commanding right and forbidding wrong.
rows.anchor: غيره: (بركته (¬6) الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر) (¬7).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God charged him to establish prayer and pay zakah; zakah may mean financial almsgiving or purification from sins and avoidance of disobedience.
rows.anchor: {وأوصاني} أمرني، وتقدم إلى {بالصلاة} بإقامتها {والزكاة} أي:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus was dutiful and gentle toward his mother; this phrase coordinates with مباركا.
rows.anchor: - {وبرا بوالدتي} مطيعا لها لطيفا بها، وهو عطف على {مباركا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says Jesus's mention of his mother but not a father showed people that his origin was a divine act.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: (لما قال: {وبرا بوالدتي} ولم يقل: بوالدي علموا أنه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jabbar means arrogant, killing or striking in anger; shaqi means disobedient to his Lord.
rows.anchor: متعظما يقتل ويضرب على الغضب

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: The definite article in السلام is more fitting because the preceding mention used indefinite سلام; here it means complete safety.
rows.anchor: لما جرى ذكر السلام قبل هذا بغير ألف ولام كان الأحسن أن يذكر ثانية بالألف واللام

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They understand God's protection at Jesus's birth to include freedom from Satan's touch; a prophetic report says Satan touches each newborn except Jesus, where the barrier intervened.
rows.anchor: السلامة علي من الله تعالى يوم ولدت حتى لم يضرني شيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse repeats the account of peace given for Yahya earlier in this surah.
rows.anchor: والآية مفسرة في قصة يحيى في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
rows.claim: Jesus said this to them, then did not speak again until children ordinarily begin to speak.
rows.anchor: كلمهم عيسى بهذا ثم سكت فلم يتكلم حتى بلغ المدة التي يتكلم فيها الصبيان

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: The child who said that he was God's servant is Jesus son of Mary, not what Christians claim, that he is God's son or a deity.
rows.anchor: أبو إسحاق: (أي ذلك الذي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He takes الحق in قول الحق to mean God; the phrase can describe Jesus as God's word, since a word is a saying.
rows.anchor: مجاهد (¬5). ويرتفع (قول) على أنه نعت لعيسى (¬6)،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قول can be nominative as an adjective of Jesus, or an annexation meaning the true saying, like حق اليقين, وعد الصدق, and الدار الآخرة; it may also predicate an understood statement.
rows.anchor: والكلمة قول، ويجوز أن يضاف القول إلى الحق (¬7)، ومعناه: القول الحق،

rows.speaker: قارئ قول الحق بالنصب
rows.claim: The accusative reading parses قول as a verbal noun: he uttered the true saying.
rows.anchor: قول الحق، ومن قرأ: قول الحق، بالنصب فهو نصب على المصدر

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: He explains the accusative as an emphatic verbal noun implicit in the preceding assertion: this is the true truth.
rows.anchor: أبو علي: (أما النصب فهو أن قوله: {ذلك عيسى ابن مريم} هو

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He allows the accusative to describe Jesus by comparison with an adjective used as an accusative circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: وإن نصبت القول وهو في النية من نعت عيسى كان صوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذي modifies Jesus; those who dispute about him doubt and disagree, with some saying he is God's son and others that he is God.
rows.anchor: تعالى: {الذي} هو هو من نعت عيسى {فيه يمترون} أي: يشكون فيختلفون،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next statement denies that God takes a child.
rows.anchor: ويقول آخر: هو الله (¬6). ثم # نفى عن نفسه اتخاذ الولد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot take a child because a child is of the parent's kind, whereas nothing resembles God; taking a child is not fitting to His attributes.
rows.anchor: لأن الولد مجانس للوالد، وكذلك من اتخذ ولدا إنما يتخذه من جنسه

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: One grammatical explanation treats the lām as displaced, yielding the sense that it is not for a child to take God.
rows.anchor: أن هذه من المقلوب على معنى ما كان للولد أن يتخذه الله

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: A second explanation makes the lām stand for the verb ينبغي: it is not proper or sound for God to take a child.
rows.anchor: أن المعنى ما كان ينبغي لله أن يتخذ من ولد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The particle من is emphatic and negates every child, one or many.
rows.anchor: الزجاج: ({من} مؤكدة تدل على نفي الواحد والجماعة)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's creation of Jesus without a father followed His command, as when He created Adam without either father or mother; whoever He wills to create comes to be, as in 3:59.
rows.anchor: كما فعل بآدم إذ خلقه من غير أب ولا أم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: For the fatha reading of أن, one analysis coordinates it with Jesus's identity statement as a nominative clause.
rows.anchor: الفراء في فتح {أن} ثلاثة أوجه أحدها: العطف على عيسى بن مريم،

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: He prefers construing the fatha as causal: because God is my Lord and yours, worship Him.
rows.anchor: ولأن الله ربي ربكم [فاعبدوه، فيعمل فيه فاعبدوه] (¬1) وهذا الوجه اختيار

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: A fourth transmitted parse supplies قضى: God decreed that He is my Lord and yours.
rows.anchor: أن المعنى وقضى الله ربي وربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, the words begin a new sentence connected to Jesus's prior statement; a reading attributed to Ubay has أن الله ربي وربكم without the conjunction.
rows.anchor: وهو: أن المعنى وقضى الله ربي وربكم (¬3)، ومن كسر استأنف الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On all parses, this verse is part of Jesus's speech to his people; the straight path is the way leading to Paradise through worship of God as commanded.
rows.anchor: وعلى الأوجه كلها الآية من كلام عيسى لقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parties are Christian sects disputing over Jesus: some called him God, some God's son, and some one of three.
rows.anchor: اختلفوا في عيسى فقال بعضهم: هو الله (¬1)، وقال بعضهم: ابن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in من بينهم is extra and means among them; the exegetes say the groups disagreed among themselves about Jesus.
rows.anchor: {من بينهم} أي: بينهم، ومن زائدة. قال المفسرون: (كانوا أحزابا متفرقين {بينهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Woe is the severe punishment of those who disbelieve by calling the Messiah God's son or a deity; mashhad may mean the witnessing of the great day or their presence there for reckoning.
rows.anchor: فشدة عذاب للذين كفروا بالله بقولهم في المسيح بأنه ابن الله وأنه إله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: On Judgment Day they hear and see when hearing and sight can no longer benefit them.
rows.anchor: سمعوا حين لم ينفعهم السمع وأبصروا حين لم ينفعهم البصر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والمفسرون
rows.claim: They render the expression as how keenly they will hear and see on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: ما أسمعهم وأبصرهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He takes hearing as obedience and sight as recognition of the truth that Jesus is neither God, God's son, nor one of three; the author calls the obedience sense good.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: (يقول: ما أبصرهم بالهدى يوم القيامة، وأطوعهم أن عيسى ليس الله،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Though deaf and blind to truth in worldly life, they will then see and hear it clearly.
rows.anchor: لئن كانوا في الدنيا صما عميا عن الحق فما أبصرهم به وأسمعهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression is an exclamation meaning how well they hear and see; Arabic has two exclamation patterns, with earlier discussion at 2:175.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {أسمع بهم وأبصر} لفظ التعجب كما قالوا في تفسيره:

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The apparent imperative form functions as a future report, not a command: hearing and sight cannot be ordered; he compares the construction at 19:75.
rows.anchor: وهذا مثال الأمر أقيم مقام الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase with bāʾ is syntactically nominative because the person marveled at occupies the subject position, as with وكفى بالله.
rows.anchor: وموضع الباء مع ما بعدها من المنجر في قولك أكرم يزيد رفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is to warn Meccan disbelievers of the regretful Day: sinners will regret not doing good and the good will regret not doing more.
rows.anchor: خوف يا محمد كفار مكة يوم الندامة يتحسر المسيء هلا أحسن العمل

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل التأويل
rows.claim: They identify the day of regret with death being slaughtered between the two groups and the announcement that the people of Paradise and Hell remain forever; the living would die of joy or grief if they could.
rows.anchor: أكثر أهل التأويل: (يعني الحسرة حين يذبح الموت بين الفريقين، ويقال: يا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He says the people of Hell would die of grief at that announcement were it not for God's decree that they remain there; this is also transmitted from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لولا ما قضى الله من تخليد أهل النار فيها لماتوا حسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the matter is decided, reckoning is over and each group has entered its destination; a past-tense verb portrays the certain future as already accomplished, as at 7:50.
rows.anchor: هو أي: فرغ من الحساب، وأدخل أهل الجنة الجنة، وأهل النار النار.

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: He interprets the matter being decided as death being slaughtered.
rows.anchor: ابن جريج في قوله: ({إذ قضي الأمر} إذ ذبح الموت)

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: He takes it as the punishment decreed for them in the afterlife while they remain heedless in worldly life.
rows.anchor: إذ قضي لهم العذاب في الآخرة وهم في الدنيا في غفلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Their heedlessness is in worldly life.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: (يريد في الدنيا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وهم في غفلة begins a fresh report that they are heedless of that day and its events; they do not believe in resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهذا استئاف إخبار عنهم أنهم في غفلة عن ذلك اليوم وأحكامه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: They are heedless in this life of what happens to death on that day and do not believe in its fate.
rows.anchor: وهم في غفلة في الدنيا عما يصنع الموت ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inherits the earth by causing its inhabitants to die; compare the statement that God is the inheritor in 15:23. The dead are then revived and returned for reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: نرث الأرض} أي: نميت سكانها فنرثها # ومن عليها لأني أميتهم وأهلكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inheritance means that people die, the earth remains, and only God owns it.
rows.anchor: يموتون وتبقى الأرض لا مالك لها إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to recount Abraham's story to them; Ibn Abbas says they knew his religion and that he was their ancestor, a true monotheist.
rows.anchor: - قوله تعالى: {واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم} اقصص عليهم قصته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Siddiq is an intensive noun for someone exceptionally truthful; the author notes this has been explained earlier.
rows.anchor: وهو معنى قوله: {إنه كان صديقا نبيا} والصديق: اسم للمبالغ في الصدق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative ending in يا أبت was discussed at the start of Joseph; Abraham rebukes his father for worshipping an idol without hearing or sight that can avert harm or help.
rows.anchor: {لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر} يعني الصنم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The knowledge Abraham received means certainty and recognition of God.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: (من اليقين والمعرفة بالله)

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abraham's statement that knowledge came to him indicates that he had received revelation.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أنه كان قد آتاه الوحي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Following Abraham means following what came to him from his Lord so that the father will be guided to a straight religion.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: (يريد اتبعني على جاءني من ربي أرشدك إلى دين مستقيم)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Not worshipping Satan means not obeying him.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: (لا تطعه) (¬5). قال أبو إسحاق: (معنى

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Worship of Satan means obeying his enticements toward unbelief and sins; worshipping an idol is worshipping Satan because obeying anything in disobedience to God is worship.
rows.anchor: أبو إسحاق: (معنى عبادة الشيطان: طاعته فيما يسول من الكفر والمعاصي)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say كان is extra; another view says it means became. The correct interpretation is present state, as in 19:8.
rows.anchor: قيل: كان زائدة. وقيل: أنه بمعنى صار (¬7). والصحيح: أنه بمعنى الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عصي means disobedient, on the faʿīl pattern used as an adjective, like other intensive forms.
rows.anchor: بلغت} [مريم: 8] الآية. والعصي: بمعنى العاصي على فعيل مثل القادر والقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham fears that his father will suffer God's punishment by obeying Satan and become Satan's companion in Hell.
rows.anchor: أخشى أن يصيبك عذاب الله بطاعتك الشيطان

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He says أخاف can mean I know, comparing it to خشينا in the story of Moses and the servant, where it means we knew.
rows.anchor: الفراء: ({أخاف} أي: أعلم، كقوله: {فخشينا أن يرهقهما} [الكهف: 80]، أي: فعلمنا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His father asks whether Abraham is deliberately turning away from his gods; رغب عن means intentionally leaving something. Ending means refrain from the forbidden act, here abusing and insulting them.
rows.anchor: رغب عن الشيء إذا تركه عمدا

rows.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل والسدي والكلبي ومجاهد وابن جريج
rows.claim: They interpret I will stone you as I will insult you with vile speech; al-Zajjaj prefers this usage of throwing or stoning someone as a euphemism for cursing.
rows.anchor: الضحاك، ومقاتل، والسدي، والكلبي، ومجاهد، وابن جريج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، رواية عطاء
rows.claim: He interprets the threat as I will kill you.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (لأقتلنك)

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He takes it literally as throwing stones until Abraham goes away; another report from Ibn Abbas says he would strike him with stones.
rows.anchor: لأرمينك بالحجارة حتى تبعد عني

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: He gives distinct usages for hajar: a man may move far away, while in fasting the related word refers to a kind of abstention.
rows.anchor: هجر الرجل هجرا إذا تباعد ونأى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He interprets abandon me as keep away from me; al-Kalbi says leave me.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: (واعتزلني) (¬4). وقال الكلبي: (واتركني) (¬5).

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، رواية عطاء
rows.claim: He takes مَلِيّا to mean for a while, as does Mujahid; Ikrima says a long duration, as do Hasan and al-Kalbi, while al-Suddi says forever.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (يريد حينا)

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: The adjective maliya denotes a long stretch of time.
rows.anchor: الملي من الدهر حين طويل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He lists dialectal forms for a long period, all derived from length; related words for delaying and extending time occur in the Quran and Arabic poetry.
rows.anchor: الفراء: (يقال: ملوة من الدهر، وملوة، وملوة، وملاوة، وملاوة وكله من الطول)

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: He explains it as an ample span of time, an adjective used as a noun, and discusses its morphology through the dropping of a radical in diminutive form.
rows.anchor: أبو علي الفارسي: (قالوا انتظرته مليا من الدهر، أي: متسعا منه، وهو

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، رواية عطاء
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation says sound in character and unharmed by me, also reported from Qatada, Atiyya, and al-Dahhak.
rows.anchor: سالم العرض لا يصيبك مني مكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the first temporal meaning, since a person ample or capable in a matter is originally spelled with hamzah; no reader transmitted the hamzated form here.
rows.anchor: فلان ملئ بهذا الأمر. والقول هو الأول؛ لأن الملي بالأمر أصله الهمز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham means that his father is safe from harm by him; he does not have an order to fight his father over unbelief.
rows.anchor: سلمت مني لا أصيبك بمكروه

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: He permits greeting non-Muslims in wartime but not in peace, citing the command to treat noncombatants kindly and Abraham as an example; Abraham's model explicitly excludes asking forgiveness, not greeting.
rows.anchor: سفيان بن عيينة: (أيجوز السلام على أهل الذمة؟ فقال: نعم، إنما حضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham promises to pray for repentance and monotheism as well as forgiveness, since forgiveness cannot be granted while his father persists in associationism; when his father's enmity to God became clear, Abraham disavowed him.
rows.anchor: سأسأل الله لك توبة تنال بها مغفرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Abraham promised before knowing prayer for a person persisting in unbelief was forbidden, then stopped after God informed him.
rows.anchor: وعد أباه الاستغفار وهو لا يعلم أن ذلك محظور على المصر على الكفر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: They explain حفيا as kind and gentle, as do most exegetes; al-Zajjaj cites the verb for treating someone kindly.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس، ومقاتل: (لطيفا بارا)]

rows.speaker: الكلبي وابن عباس، رواية عطاء
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes حفيا mean knowing; Jabir says it means a helper, and al-Farra reports both interpretations.
rows.anchor: (¬5). والكلام في هذا قد مر مستقصى في قوله: {يسألونك كأنك حفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word was discussed more fully at 7:187.
rows.anchor: والكلام في هذا قد مر مستقصى في قوله: {يسألونك كأنك حفي عنها}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham will withdraw from his people and from the idols they worship, worshipping his Lord and hoping not to be wretched by prayer; this implies their idols bring misery because they neither help nor answer prayer.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وأعتزلكم} أي: أتنحى عنكم وأفارقكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham emigrated away from them toward Syria; God comforted him for their loss by granting noble sons Isaac and Jacob, making each a prophet.
rows.anchor: هاجرهم بالخروج إلى ناحية الشام

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: The mercy given to Abraham's family means wealth and children; most exegetes explain it as abundant worldly provision.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: (المال والولد) (¬3). وهو قول الأكثرين قالوا: (رحمته

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view takes the gift of mercy as Scripture and prophethood.
rows.anchor: آخرون: (يعني الكتاب والنبوة) (¬5). {وجعلنا لهم لسان صدق}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase من رحمتنا is in the accusative as the object of the gift.
rows.anchor: من سعة الرزق) (¬4). فقوله: {من رحمتنا} في محل النصب بوقوع الهبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A high tongue of truth means elevated, lasting good praise; all religious communities honor Abraham and his descendants. Tongue denotes speech or language, and adding truth is praise, as in the cited expressions at 10:93 and 10:2.
rows.anchor: لسان صدق} أي: ثناء حسنا في الناس {عليا} مرتفعا سائرا في الناس

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: With kasra on the lām, Moses sincerely devoted worship and monotheism to God, free of anything that would corrupt it.
rows.anchor: أخلص العبادة والتوحيد لله تعالى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He says Moses made himself wholly devoted to obedience to God, without stain.
rows.anchor: جعل نفسه خالصة في طاعة الله غير دنسه

rows.speaker: قارئ مخلصا بالفتح
rows.claim: With fatḥ on the lām, God made Moses chosen and pure of blemish; the two readings are supported respectively by 4:146 and 38:46.
rows.anchor: فهو الذي أخلصه الله وجعله مختارا خالصا من الدنس
